entry.title: Gateway to Ojúbọ Òṣogbo
entry.note: The 2022 panorama fixes the camera and the stair-side facing. Reconstructed side returns and carved piers follow the photographs. The stair approach uses terrain-relative height. Exact sculptural depths and slopes outside the platform remain estimates.

terrainReference.basis: Sampled along the stair axis just beyond the bottom tread at local [0, 4.62] m.

panoramaRegistration.method: Applied a shape correction to the existing silhouette controls at a fixed camera pose and published heading. The reduced residual measures the fitted controls and is not an independent site survey.

terrain.source: Native Terrarium grid used by World Explorer

terrainReference.basis: Sampled along the stair axis just beyond the bottom tread at local [0, 4.62] m.

observations: The geolocated panorama resolves the signed stair-side facing. Floor contacts and gable cutouts constrain the reconstructed portal widths. The PMTiles comparison finds no mapped road, building or water overlaps.
All fifteen sampled tread points clear the unmodified terrain in all four LODs. The lowest risers and side faces extend into the native field where it slopes.
The fixture checks the map environment without replacing PMTiles features. Two comparison angles include the separate First Palace draft.
The reported pixel difference is a fit to approximate control points. The depths of the carvings and unmapped enclosure remain estimated.

The current close-up uses curved clay crests, molded arch undersides and solid relief figures on both faces of the central piers. The prior registered camera and photographed silhouette controls remain the placement basis.

entry.title: Gateway to Ojúbọ Òṣogbo
entry.note: Trial only. The Trust photograph shows a roof through the central gate. This layout tests the gate 20 m in front of the draft First Palace, stairs toward the court. Offsets, exact identity of the roof visible through the arch, location, signed facing and grades remain provisional.

relativeLayout.basis: The photographs document a roofline through the central gate. The trial substitutes the adjacent First Palace at its existing draft location and tests one plausible separation and facing. Neither the relative offset nor the identity of the roof and the signed facing are measured.

trialGrade.name: Gateway placement trial
trialGrade.basis: Test terrain contact with the narrow stair landing, allowing approximately 0.7 m rise toward the approach. This is an illustrative grade, not a survey.

observations: Both models render together in each level. The close view shows the First Palace through the central portal in the trial layout.
Without grading, one shoulder and the bottom step are buried at this anchor. The graded treads clear the DEM in the center, with residual shoulder intersections along the edges in the oblique view.
The trial retained both mapped roads, the river and both landcover features. Unloading released the landmark geometry.
The trial tests a relative layout. Overhead canopy still hides the footprint and the values do not establish its geographic placement.

archiveLocationTrial.scanGeoReference: The metadata projection is empty. The approximate map rectangles are supplied separately by Open Heritage 3D.
archiveLocationTrial.notes: The second fit trial uses the First Palace scan map rectangle and places the gateway a provisional 20 m in front. The palace is visible through the central opening. Raw terrain clears the central stair but covers its west shoulder by 0.44 m. The gateway origin, facing and grade still lack independent controls.

gateTrial.title: Gateway to Ojúbọ Òṣogbo
gateTrial.note: Trial of the relative position of First Palace marker 8 and Ojubo Oshun Entrance marker 35. The signed gate bearing aims the stair side at the palace for the sightline check.

entranceMarkerTrial.notes: The archived aerial scan area and Figure 1 markers 8 and 35 produce a 63 m southwest gateway trial. This places the gate base 5.8 m higher than the palace and brings the terrace to the edge of a mapped road. In the through-arch view the terrain hides the palace facade. The separately tested 20 m layout shows that facade. The photograph shows only part of a roof through the opening, and its identity remains uncertain. The published marker helps narrow the search area. Both trial poses remain provisional.
